compute.model: per-resource, charged only while the machine is running
compute.minimum: No minimum charge published; runtime is metered per second only while running

notes.claim: Runtime is metered by the second, only while running.
notes.quote: Runtime is metered by the second, only while a machine is running.

notes.claim: You pay for the size you allocated, not the CPU you used.
notes.quote: While a machine is running, you pay for the vCPUs and memory you gave it.
Pause it, and you just pay for storage.

notes.claim: Plans include monthly credits that do not carry over.
notes.quote: Usage comes out of your included credits first, then you pay as you go. Credits reset every month.

notes.claim: Sizes are fixed vCPU/RAM pairs by plan.
notes.quote: Machine size | 4 vCPUs and 8 GiB of memory by default, the only size on the free plan. Pro: 2/4, 4/8 or 8/16. Team: 2/4 up to 32 vCPUs / 64 GiB.

notes.claim: No lifetime timeout on paid machines; the free plan's max-run is fixed at 480 minutes.
notes.quote: max-run <id-or-name> <minutes> pause after that many running minutes, even while active; -1: unlimited, 0: now (free plan: fixed at 480)

notes.claim: The same unit rates apply on every paid plan; plans differ in credits and limits, not in per-resource price.
notes.quote: Paid plans pay these for usage beyond their monthly credits.

derivedExample.note: Derived from the published unit rates; the pricing page's own calculator shows the same compute-only figure and excludes storage.
derivedExample.quote: vCPU | $0.004 | per vCPU-hour … Memory | $0.00225 | per GiB-hour

storage.model: one persistent /data disk per machine plus snapshot bytes, all billed as stored GiB-hours

disk.includedGiB: 20 GiB /data comes with the machine; free plan capped at 200 GB stored data

billedWhileStoppedOrPaused.value: Yes. Paused or stopped machines keep their disks and continue to bill storage.
billedWhileStoppedOrPaused.quote: Storage still counts toward plan limits and billing

snapshots.value: Snapshots are stored bytes at the same GiB-hour storage rate; no separate snapshot price. Free plan allows 5 snapshots.
snapshots.quote: Snapshots | Free: 5. Pro and Team: unlimited

retention.value: No forced TTL; stays until you delete it
retention.quote: **No forced TTL.** A paused or stopped machine and every snapshot you save stay until **you** delete them.

retention.case: Workspace disabled for non-payment or cancellation
retention.value: Machines and snapshots kept 30 days, then deleted
retention.quote: a workspace **disabled** (its subscription cancelled, or unpaid past the grace period) keeps its machines and snapshots for 30 days, then they are deleted

diskGrowth.value: 1-1024 GiB; grow while running, shrink only while stopped; plan caps 200 GiB Pro, 500 GiB Builder, 1024 GiB Team/Enterprise
diskGrowth.quote: The disk may grow to at most 200 GiB on Pro, 500 GiB on Builder, 1024 GiB on Team and Enterprise

egress.sendCap: about 50 Mbit/s per VM (~6 MB/s); downloads into the VM are not capped
egress.quote: Ingress is always free. Each plan includes egress every month (100 GiB on Free, 1 TiB on Pro, 5 TiB on Builder, 50 TiB on Team), then $0.02 per GiB.

other.value: No IPv4 product; ports are published as HTTPS URLs

hermes.route: Manual only. Create a machine from the agent-browser template (Debian with Node, Docker and a desktop), open its Terminal tab or SSH in, install Hermes Agent from its own repository, set the model key, and keep it running with systemd or a background job; publish the port it serves.
hermes.officialTemplateOrGuide: not found: no Hermes template, one-click or InstaBox guide
hermes.manualSteps: 1) Dashboard → Machines → Create machine (agent-browser). 2) Open the Terminal tab or `instabox ssh`. 3) Install Hermes Agent and its dependencies. 4) Add the model/API key. 5) Run it under systemd or `exec --background`. 6) Publish its port with `instabox port publish`.
hermes.nonCoderFromDashboard: Partly. The dashboard can create the machine and open a browser terminal or desktop, but there is no guided Hermes install, so someone must type the install and service commands.

quotes.quote: In the dashboard, **Create machine** on the **Machines** page does what `instabox create` does.
`~/.bashrc` only reaches interactive shells (SSH, the Terminal tab)

openclaw.route: Manual only, same route as Hermes; no OpenClaw template or guide found.
openclaw.manualSteps: Same as Hermes: create an agent-browser machine, install OpenClaw in its terminal, configure the gateway and model key, run it as a service, publish its port.
openclaw.nonCoderFromDashboard: Partly, for the same reason: machine creation and a browser terminal exist, but the install is manual.

quotes.quote: Open a machine and choose the **Computer** tab. Click the desktop to take control; it goes back to the agent after a minute idle.
